b-carotene-binding proteins have been found in bovine liver and intestine and in livers of the rat and ferret. In addition, a xantho-
phyll-binding protein has been found in human retina and macula. Carotenoids are also present in nature as crystalline aggregates
(lycopene in chromoplasts) or as ﬁne dispersions in aqueous media (b-carotene in oranges). Typically carotenoid molecules are
very sensitive to elevated temperatures and to the presence of oxygen, acid, and light when in solution, and are subject to oxida-
tive degradation (Meléndez et al., 2019).
